# `sec-js/no-unsafe-regex`

**No regular expression that can run for ever, no regular expression built from a request**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-security-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-security-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (what the pattern should accept is a decision for the author) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Security** | CWE-1333 · OWASP A06:2025 · security severity `medium` |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-security/detect-unsafe-regex`, `eslint-plugin-security/detect-non-literal-regexp` |

## What it checks

A regular expression has no quantified group that itself holds a quantifier (`(a+)+`), and `new RegExp(…)` is not built from request data.

**Why:** A nested quantifier gives the engine exponentially many ways to match a near-miss, so a short string freezes the process (ReDoS, CWE-1333); a pattern the client writes does the same on purpose.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-security-js
pip install codelaw-rules-security-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:sec-js/strict` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:sec-js/strict"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"sec-js/no-unsafe-regex" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "sec-js/no-unsafe-regex" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"sec-js/no-unsafe-regex" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"sec-js/no-unsafe-regex" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"sec-js/no-unsafe-regex" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "sec-js/no-unsafe-regex": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-js/no-unsafe-regex: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore sec-js/no-unsafe-regex expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule sec-js/no-unsafe-regex --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain sec-js/no-unsafe-regex       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule sec-js/no-unsafe-regex  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>          # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Rewrite the pattern so no two parts can match the same text: `(a+)+` is `a+`.
2. Escape request data before it goes into a pattern: `value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")`.
3. Cap the length of the input, or use an engine without backtracking (`re2`).

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
const valid = /^(a+)+$/.test(input);
```

#### Do

```js
const valid = /^a+$/.test(input);
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
const valid = /^(a+)+$/.test(input);
```

#### Do

```jsx
const valid = /^a+$/.test(input);
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
const valid = /^(a+)+$/.test(input);
```

#### Do

```ts
const valid = /^a+$/.test(input);
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
const valid = /^(a+)+$/.test(input);
```

#### Do

```tsx
const valid = /^a+$/.test(input);
```
